-- Non-blocking: two MSHRs (miss registers), as in the CcNoc stage-2 L1
-- (L1NB.lean). A load that misses takes a free MSHR and asks memory; a load
-- to a line that already has an MSHR is a secondary miss and waits on it
-- (merged: no second request); a hit is answered at once even while misses
-- are outstanding. Memory answers one MSHR per cycle (fill_valid, fill_idx).
-- Answers here are not ordered: resp_tag says which load it is.
xblue typedef struct { Bool valid; Bit#(4) line; Bit#(2) waiters; } Mshr;

xblue module mkTwoMSHRs;
  input Bool reset;
  input Bool ld_valid;
  input Bit#(4) ld_line;
  input Bit#(2) ld_tag;
  input Bool fill_valid;
  input Bit#(1) fill_idx;

  RegFile#(Bit#(4), Bool) present <- mkRegFileFull;    -- which lines are cached
  Reg#(Vector#(2, Mshr)) mshr <- mkReg(0);
  Reg#(Bit#(32)) merged <- mkReg(0);                   -- secondary misses so far

  Bool hit = present.sub(ld_line);
  Bool m0 = mshr[0].valid && mshr[0].line == ld_line;
  Bool m1 = mshr[1].valid && mshr[1].line == ld_line;
  Bool secondary = m0 || m1;
  Bool free0 = !mshr[0].valid;
  Bool free1 = !mshr[1].valid;

  -- a load is taken unless it misses with both MSHRs busy on other lines
  method Bool ld_ready = hit || secondary || free0 || free1;
  method Bool resp_valid = ld_valid && hit;
  method Bit#(2) resp_tag = ld_tag;
  method Bool mem_req = ld_valid && !hit && !secondary && (free0 || free1);
  method Bit#(4) mem_line = ld_line;
  method Bit#(32) secondary_misses = merged;

  rule fill (fill_valid && mshr[fill_idx].valid);
    present.upd(mshr[fill_idx].line, 1);
    mshr[fill_idx] <= Mshr { valid: 1'b0 };
  endrule
  rule load (ld_valid && !hit);
    if (m0) mshr[0] <= mshr[0] with { waiters = mshr[0].waiters + 1 };
    else if (m1) mshr[1] <= mshr[1] with { waiters = mshr[1].waiters + 1 };
    else if (free0) mshr[0] <= Mshr { valid: 1'b1, line: ld_line, waiters: 2'd1 };
    else if (free1) mshr[1] <= Mshr { valid: 1'b1, line: ld_line, waiters: 2'd1 };
    if (secondary) merged <= merged + 1;
  endrule
  rule clear (reset);
    mshr <= 0;
  endrule
  -- load first: it sees the MSHRs as the methods ld_ready and mem_req saw them
  -- at the start of the cycle, so a fill cannot free one under its feet
  schedule load ≫ fill ≫ clear;
endmodule
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- reasoning
open XBlue

structure Regs where
  mshr : BitVec 14      -- two entries of 7 bits: valid, line (4), waiters (2)
  merged : BitVec 32

/-- One clock cycle of the design itself: the registers after it, and the outputs
    `mem_req` and `ld_ready`. `present` is the array, read at the start of the cycle. -/
def step (reset ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (tag : BitVec 2) (fillValid : BitVec 1)
    (fillIdx : BitVec 1) (present : BitVec 16) (s : Regs) : Regs × BitVec 1 × BitVec 1 :=
  let t := mkTwoMSHRs.design.cycle
      (.cons reset (.cons ldValid (.cons line (.cons tag (.cons fillValid (.cons fillIdx .nil))))))
      (.cons s.mshr (.cons s.merged .nil)) (.cons present .nil)
  (⟨t.regs.get mkTwoMSHRs.mshr, t.regs.get mkTwoMSHRs.merged⟩, t.wires.get mkTwoMSHRs.mem_req,
    t.wires.get mkTwoMSHRs.ld_ready)

-- An entry is `valid ++ line ++ waiters`.
def valid (e : BitVec 7) : Bool := e.extractLsb' 6 1 = 1#1

def lineOf (e : BitVec 7) : BitVec 4 := e.extractLsb' 2 4

def bump (e : BitVec 7) : BitVec 7 := e.extractLsb' 2 5 ++ (e.extractLsb' 0 2 + 1#2)

def fresh (line : BitVec 4) : BitVec 7 := 1#1 ++ line ++ 1#2

-- One plain function per rule, and per method.
/-- `load`: merge into the MSHR for this line, or take a free one. `hit` is the
    `present` array's entry for the line, read at the start of the cycle. -/
def loadStep (ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (hit : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let m0 := valid e0 && lineOf e0 == line
  let m1 := valid e1 && lineOf e1 == line
  let go := ldValid = 1#1 ∧ hit = 0#1
  let l0 := if go ∧ m0 then bump e0 else if go ∧ !m0 ∧ !m1 ∧ !valid e0 then fresh line else e0
  let l1 := if go ∧ !m0 ∧ m1 then bump e1
            else if go ∧ !m0 ∧ !m1 ∧ valid e0 ∧ !valid e1 then fresh line else e1
  ⟨l1 ++ l0, if go ∧ (m0 ∨ m1) then s.merged + 1#32 else s.merged⟩
/-- `fill`: memory answers one MSHR, which becomes free. -/
def fillStep (fillValid fillIdx : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let f0 := if fillValid = 1#1 ∧ fillIdx = 0#1 ∧ valid e0 then 0#7 else e0
  let f1 := if fillValid = 1#1 ∧ fillIdx = 1#1 ∧ valid e1 then 0#7 else e1
  ⟨f1 ++ f0, s.merged⟩
def clearStep (reset : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
  ⟨if reset = 1#1 then 0#14 else s.mshr, s.merged⟩
/-- The methods are computed from the registers at the start of the cycle. -/
def memReqOf (ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (hit : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : BitVec 1 :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let secondary := (valid e0 && lineOf e0 == line) || (valid e1 && lineOf e1 == line)
  if ldValid = 1#1 ∧ hit = 0#1 ∧ !secondary ∧ (!valid e0 || !valid e1) then 1#1 else 0#1
def ldReadyOf (line : BitVec 4) (hit : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : BitVec 1 :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let secondary := (valid e0 && lineOf e0 == line) || (valid e1 && lineOf e1 == line)
  if hit = 1#1 ∨ secondary ∨ !valid e0 ∨ !valid e1 then 1#1 else 0#1

/-- The cycle is the schedule `load ≫ fill ≫ clear`, with the methods read from
    the start of the cycle. -/
theorem step_eq_steps (reset ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (tag : BitVec 2) (fillValid fillIdx : BitVec 1)
    (present : BitVec 16) (s : Regs) :
    step reset ldValid line tag fillValid fillIdx present s =
      (clearStep reset (fillStep fillValid fillIdx (loadStep ldValid line (Memory.readVal present line) s)),
       memReqOf ldValid line (Memory.readVal present line) s, ldReadyOf line (Memory.readVal present line) s) := by
  obtain ⟨m, mg⟩ := s
  -- unfold the design's cycle, name the rules and methods, then check the bits
  simp [step, mkTwoMSHRs.design, Design.cycle, mkTwoMSHRs.schedule,
     mkTwoMSHRs.interfaces, mkTwoMSHRs.rules.load, mkTwoMSHRs.rules.fill, mkTwoMSHRs.rules.clear,
     mkTwoMSHRs.values.hit, mkTwoMSHRs.values.m0, mkTwoMSHRs.values.m1, mkTwoMSHRs.values.secondary,
     mkTwoMSHRs.values.free0, mkTwoMSHRs.values.free1, mkTwoMSHRs.signature, Sched.run, Action.step,
     Action.fires, writesIf, arrayWritesIf, State.write, State.cur, State.read, HList.set, HList.get,
     Expr.eval, Expr.binVal, Expr.cmpVal, RExpr.readArray, Common.putR, Common.putW, Common.memAt,
     Common.zeros, mkTwoMSHRs.mshr, mkTwoMSHRs.merged, mkTwoMSHRs.reset, mkTwoMSHRs.ld_valid,
     mkTwoMSHRs.ld_line, mkTwoMSHRs.ld_tag, mkTwoMSHRs.fill_valid, mkTwoMSHRs.fill_idx,
     mkTwoMSHRs.present, mkTwoMSHRs.ld_ready, mkTwoMSHRs.resp_valid, mkTwoMSHRs.resp_tag,
     mkTwoMSHRs.mem_req, mkTwoMSHRs.mem_line, mkTwoMSHRs.secondary_misses, sliceWidth] <;>
  simp only [loadStep, fillStep, clearStep, memReqOf, ldReadyOf, valid, lineOf, bump, fresh] <;>
  generalize (Memory.readVal present line : BitVec 1) = hit <;>
  bv_decide

-- Consequences, read off the story.

/-- At most one MSHR per line: a second miss to a line is merged, never allocated. -/
def Inv (s : Regs) : Prop :=
  ¬ (valid (s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7) = true ∧ valid (s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7) = true ∧
     lineOf (s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7) = lineOf (s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7))

theorem no_duplicates (reset ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (tag : BitVec 2)
    (fillValid fillIdx : BitVec 1) (present : BitVec 16) (s : Regs) (h : Inv s) :
    Inv (step reset ldValid line tag fillValid fillIdx present s).1 := by
  rw [step_eq_steps]
  obtain ⟨m, mg⟩ := s
  simp only [Inv, loadStep, fillStep, clearStep, valid, lineOf, bump, fresh] at * <;>
  generalize (Memory.readVal present line : BitVec 1) = hit <;>
  bv_decide

/-- Every new MSHR has a request behind it: if an entry is valid for a line it did
    not hold before, `mem_req` was raised. -/
theorem new_mshr_has_request (ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (tag : BitVec 2)
    (fillValid fillIdx : BitVec 1) (present : BitVec 16) (s : Regs) :
    let r := step 0#1 ldValid line tag fillValid fillIdx present s
    (valid (r.1.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7) = true →
      (valid (s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7) = false ∨ lineOf (r.1.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7) ≠ lineOf (s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7)) →
        r.2.1 = 1#1) ∧
    (valid (r.1.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7) = true →
      (valid (s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7) = false ∨ lineOf (r.1.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7) ≠ lineOf (s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7)) →
        r.2.1 = 1#1) := by
  rw [step_eq_steps]
  obtain ⟨m, mg⟩ := s
  simp only [loadStep, fillStep, clearStep, memReqOf, valid, lineOf, bump, fresh] <;>
  generalize (Memory.readVal present line : BitVec 1) = hit <;>
  constructor <;> intro h1 h2 <;> bv_decide

explain: Cycle 1: the first load to line 3 misses. 1. interfaces: free MSHR, no match, so mem_req is high. 2. load takes MSHR 0. From then on every load to line 3 finds MSHR 0: interfaces sees a match, so mem_req stays low, and load merges, which counts a secondary miss. Exactly one request goes out (cycle 1), and secondary_misses counts up from cycle 3. Without fills the line never arrives, but the cache does not stall.

    t.wires.get mkTwoMSHRs.ld_ready)

-- An entry is `valid ++ line ++ waiters`.
def valid (e : BitVec 7) : Bool := e.extractLsb' 6 1 = 1#1

def lineOf (e : BitVec 7) : BitVec 4 := e.extractLsb' 2 4

def bump (e : BitVec 7) : BitVec 7 := e.extractLsb' 2 5 ++ (e.extractLsb' 0 2 + 1#2)

def fresh (line : BitVec 4) : BitVec 7 := 1#1 ++ line ++ 1#2

-- One plain function per rule, and per method.
/-- `load`: merge into the MSHR for this line, or take a free one. `hit` is the
    `present` array's entry for the line, read at the start of the cycle. -/
def loadStep (ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (hit : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let m0 := valid e0 && lineOf e0 == line
  let m1 := valid e1 && lineOf e1 == line
  let go := ldValid = 1#1 ∧ hit = 0#1
  let l0 := if go ∧ m0 then bump e0 else if go ∧ !m0 ∧ !m1 ∧ !valid e0 then fresh line else e0
  let l1 := if go ∧ !m0 ∧ m1 then bump e1
            else if go ∧ !m0 ∧ !m1 ∧ valid e0 ∧ !valid e1 then fresh line else e1
  ⟨l1 ++ l0, if go ∧ (m0 ∨ m1) then s.merged + 1#32 else s.merged⟩
/-- `fill`: memory answers one MSHR, which becomes free. -/
def fillStep (fillValid fillIdx : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let f0 := if fillValid = 1#1 ∧ fillIdx = 0#1 ∧ valid e0 then 0#7 else e0
  let f1 := if fillValid = 1#1 ∧ fillIdx = 1#1 ∧ valid e1 then 0#7 else e1
  ⟨f1 ++ f0, s.merged⟩
def clearStep (reset : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
  ⟨if reset = 1#1 then 0#14 else s.mshr, s.merged⟩
/-- The methods are computed from the registers at the start of the cycle. -/
def memReqOf (ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (hit : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : BitVec 1 :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let secondary := (valid e0 && lineOf e0 == line) || (valid e1 && lineOf e1 == line)
  if ldValid = 1#1 ∧ hit = 0#1 ∧ !secondary ∧ (!valid e0 || !valid e1) then 1#1 else 0#1
def ldReadyOf (line : BitVec 4) (hit : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : BitVec 1 :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let secondary := (valid e0 && lineOf e0 == line) || (valid e1 && lineOf e1 == line)
  if hit = 1#1 ∨ secondary ∨ !valid e0 ∨ !valid e1 then 1#1 else 0#1

/-- The cycle is the schedule `load ≫ fill ≫ clear`, with the methods read from
    the start of the cycle. -/
theorem step_eq_steps (reset ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (tag : BitVec 2) (fillValid fillIdx : BitVec 1)
    (present : BitVec 16) (s : Regs) :
    step reset ldValid line tag fillValid fillIdx present s =
      (clearStep reset (fillStep fillValid fillIdx (loadStep ldValid line (Memory.readVal present line) s)),
       memReqOf ldValid line (Memory.readVal present line) s, ldReadyOf line (Memory.readVal present line) s) := by
  obtain ⟨m, mg⟩ := s
  -- unfold the design's cycle, name the rules and methods, then check the bits
  simp [step, mkTwoMSHRs.design, Design.cycle, mkTwoMSHRs.schedule,
     mkTwoMSHRs.interfaces, mkTwoMSHRs.rules.load, mkTwoMSHRs.rules.fill, mkTwoMSHRs.rules.clear,
     mkTwoMSHRs.values.hit, mkTwoMSHRs.values.m0, mkTwoMSHRs.values.m1, mkTwoMSHRs.values.secondary,
     mkTwoMSHRs.values.free0, mkTwoMSHRs.values.free1, mkTwoMSHRs.signature, Sched.run, Action.step,
     Action.fires, writesIf, arrayWritesIf, State.write, State.cur, State.read, HList.set, HList.get,
     Expr.eval, Expr.binVal, Expr.cmpVal, RExpr.readArray, Common.putR, Common.putW, Common.memAt,
     Common.zeros, mkTwoMSHRs.mshr, mkTwoMSHRs.merged, mkTwoMSHRs.reset, mkTwoMSHRs.ld_valid,
     mkTwoMSHRs.ld_line, mkTwoMSHRs.ld_tag, mkTwoMSHRs.fill_valid, mkTwoMSHRs.fill_idx,
     mkTwoMSHRs.present, mkTwoMSHRs.ld_ready, mkTwoMSHRs.resp_valid, mkTwoMSHRs.resp_tag,
     mkTwoMSHRs.mem_req, mkTwoMSHRs.mem_line, mkTwoMSHRs.secondary_misses, sliceWidth] <;>
  simp only [loadStep, fillStep, clearStep, memReqOf, ldReadyOf, valid, lineOf, bump, fresh] <;>
  generalize (Memory.readVal present line : BitVec 1) = hit <;>
  bv_decide

-- Consequences, read off the story.

/-- At most one MSHR per line: a second miss to a line is merged, never allocated. -/
def Inv (s : Regs) : Prop :=
  ¬ (valid (s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7) = true ∧ valid (s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7) = true ∧
     lineOf (s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7) = lineOf (s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7))

theorem no_duplicates (reset ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (tag : BitVec 2)
    (fillValid fillIdx : BitVec 1) (present : BitVec 16) (s : Regs) (h : Inv s) :
    Inv (step reset ldValid line tag fillValid fillIdx present s).1 := by
  rw [step_eq_steps]
  obtain ⟨m, mg⟩ := s
  simp only [Inv, loadStep, fillStep, clearStep, valid, lineOf, bump, fresh] at * <;>

When line 7 arrives at cycle 3: 1. interfaces: it misses, no MSHR matches, none is free, so ld_ready drops to 0. 2. load runs and finds nothing it can do. answers.source:
-- Non-blocking: two MSHRs (miss registers), as in the CcNoc stage-2 L1
-- (L1NB.lean). A load that misses takes a free MSHR and asks memory; a load
-- to a line that already has an MSHR is a secondary miss and waits on it
-- (merged: no second request); a hit is answered at once even while misses
-- are outstanding. Memory answers one MSHR per cycle (fill_valid, fill_idx).
-- Answers here are not ordered: resp_tag says which load it is.
xblue typedef struct { Bool valid; Bit#(4) line; Bit#(2) waiters; } Mshr;

xblue module mkTwoMSHRs;
  input Bool reset;
  input Bool ld_valid;
  input Bit#(4) ld_line;
  input Bit#(2) ld_tag;
  input Bool fill_valid;
  input Bit#(1) fill_idx;

  RegFile#(Bit#(4), Bool) present <- mkRegFileFull;    -- which lines are cached
  Reg#(Vector#(2, Mshr)) mshr <- mkReg(0);
  Reg#(Bit#(32)) merged <- mkReg(0);                   -- secondary misses so far

  Bool hit = present.sub(ld_line);
  Bool m0 = mshr[0].valid && mshr[0].line == ld_line;
  Bool m1 = mshr[1].valid && mshr[1].line == ld_line;
  Bool secondary = m0 || m1;
  Bool free0 = !mshr[0].valid;
  Bool free1 = !mshr[1].valid;

  -- a load is taken unless it misses with both MSHRs busy on other lines
  method Bool ld_ready = hit || secondary || free0 || free1;
  method Bool resp_valid = ld_valid && hit;
  method Bit#(2) resp_tag = ld_tag;
  method Bool mem_req = ld_valid && !hit && !secondary && (free0 || free1);
  method Bit#(4) mem_line = ld_line;
  method Bit#(32) secondary_misses = merged;

  rule fill (fill_valid && mshr[fill_idx].valid);
    present.upd(mshr[fill_idx].line, 1);
    mshr[fill_idx] <= Mshr { valid: 1'b0 };
  endrule
  rule load (ld_valid && !hit);
    if (m0) mshr[0] <= mshr[0] with { waiters = mshr[0].waiters + 1 };
    else if (m1) mshr[1] <= mshr[1] with { waiters = mshr[1].waiters + 1 };
    else if (free0) mshr[0] <= Mshr { valid: 1'b1, line: ld_line, waiters: 2'd1 };
    else if (free1) mshr[1] <= Mshr { valid: 1'b1, line: ld_line, waiters: 2'd1 };
    if (secondary) merged <= merged + 1;
  endrule
  rule clear (reset);
    mshr <= 0;
  endrule
  -- load first: it sees the MSHRs as the methods ld_ready and mem_req saw them
  -- at the start of the cycle, so a fill cannot free one under its feet
  schedule load ≫ fill ≫ clear;
endmodule
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- reasoning
open XBlue

structure Regs where
  mshr : BitVec 14      -- two entries of 7 bits: valid, line (4), waiters (2)
  merged : BitVec 32

/-- One clock cycle of the design itself: the registers after it, and the outputs
    `mem_req` and `ld_ready`. `present` is the array, read at the start of the cycle. -/
def step (reset ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (tag : BitVec 2) (fillValid : BitVec 1)
    (fillIdx : BitVec 1) (present : BitVec 16) (s : Regs) : Regs × BitVec 1 × BitVec 1 :=
  let t := mkTwoMSHRs.design.cycle
      (.cons reset (.cons ldValid (.cons line (.cons tag (.cons fillValid (.cons fillIdx .nil))))))
      (.cons s.mshr (.cons s.merged .nil)) (.cons present .nil)
  (⟨t.regs.get mkTwoMSHRs.mshr, t.regs.get mkTwoMSHRs.merged⟩, t.wires.get mkTwoMSHRs.mem_req,
    t.wires.get mkTwoMSHRs.ld_ready)

-- An entry is `valid ++ line ++ waiters`.
def valid (e : BitVec 7) : Bool := e.extractLsb' 6 1 = 1#1

def lineOf (e : BitVec 7) : BitVec 4 := e.extractLsb' 2 4

def bump (e : BitVec 7) : BitVec 7 := e.extractLsb' 2 5 ++ (e.extractLsb' 0 2 + 1#2)

def fresh (line : BitVec 4) : BitVec 7 := 1#1 ++ line ++ 1#2

-- One plain function per rule, and per method.
/-- `load`: merge into the MSHR for this line, or take a free one. `hit` is the
    `present` array's entry for the line, read at the start of the cycle. -/
def loadStep (ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (hit : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let m0 := valid e0 && lineOf e0 == line
  let m1 := valid e1 && lineOf e1 == line
  let go := ldValid = 1#1 ∧ hit = 0#1
  let l0 := if go ∧ m0 then bump e0 else if go ∧ !m0 ∧ !m1 ∧ !valid e0 then fresh line else e0
  let l1 := if go ∧ !m0 ∧ m1 then bump e1
            else if go ∧ !m0 ∧ !m1 ∧ valid e0 ∧ !valid e1 then fresh line else e1
  ⟨l1 ++ l0, if go ∧ (m0 ∨ m1) then s.merged + 1#32 else s.merged⟩
/-- `fill`: memory answers one MSHR, which becomes free. -/
def fillStep (fillValid fillIdx : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let f0 := if fillValid = 1#1 ∧ fillIdx = 0#1 ∧ valid e0 then 0#7 else e0
  let f1 := if fillValid = 1#1 ∧ fillIdx = 1#1 ∧ valid e1 then 0#7 else e1
  ⟨f1 ++ f0, s.merged⟩
def clearStep (reset : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
  ⟨if reset = 1#1 then 0#14 else s.mshr, s.merged⟩
/-- The methods are computed from the registers at the start of the cycle. -/
def memReqOf (ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (hit : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : BitVec 1 :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let secondary := (valid e0 && lineOf e0 == line) || (valid e1 && lineOf e1 == line)
  if ldValid = 1#1 ∧ hit = 0#1 ∧ !secondary ∧ (!valid e0 || !valid e1) then 1#1 else 0#1
def ldReadyOf (line : BitVec 4) (hit : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : BitVec 1 :=
  let e0 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 0 7
  let e1 := s.mshr.extractLsb' 7 7
  let secondary := (valid e0 && lineOf e0 == line) || (valid e1 && lineOf e1 == line)
  if hit = 1#1 ∨ secondary ∨ !valid e0 ∨ !valid e1 then 1#1 else 0#1

/-- The cycle is the schedule `load ≫ fill ≫ clear`, with the methods read from
    the start of the cycle. -/
theorem step_eq_steps (reset ldValid : BitVec 1) (line : BitVec 4) (tag : BitVec 2) (fillValid fillIdx : BitVec 1)
